_: engines.least: the engines a besieging host builds on the spot at the least, whatever the bridge's companies hold (up to engines.angles). band: how far (world units) out from the wall the camp line stands (camp_r, where the companies stand and the palisade and tents begin): room for the engines' line, the besiegers' host behind it and the assault parties between (group test 1: at 1.3 a 6 m engine 13 m long and an 800-man host shared one strip). clear_of_town: the siege (its wall, breach, engines and camp; scenes.gd) stands at least this far (world units) past the town's outermost building, whatever the town's size says. The besiegers' camp and their engines (realm/scripts/siege_camp.gd; North Star docs/art/target/04-siege.jpg; Stronghold, Age of Empires II, Total War; research rule 13: three rings, the town and its wall, a band of open ground with the engines and the assault parties, the camp of tents and cook fires behind). Pitched with every siege. Distances in world units from the camp line (camp_r, where the companies stand; minus is toward the town); angles in radians either side of the camp's middle (engines.from_wall, parked.from_wall, assault.home_from_wall and storm_host.from_wall are from the wall's foot instead). assault.home_from_wall: where the six-man assault parties wait between rushes, just behind the engines' line and ahead of the host. tents: rows of tents in the besieger's colours (canvas: how far toward cream; size: width, height, length). palisade: a line of stakes and planking in front of the tents (Kenney Castle Kit), gaps where the companies go out; depth, the ground a stake length holds across the line (siege_camp.gd _set_piece: every camp piece claims its ground as camp, and is set down only where that ground is free). wagons.props_reach: how far round a wagon its barrels and crates stand, the ground it holds. fires: cook fires among the tents with men sat round them. wagons: the baggage behind. engines: in a line in the band, from_wall (world units) out from the wall's foot, ahead of the storm host; an angle whose ground is not level looks near for level ground (near: a step along the arc in radians, a step out or in, how many steps) rather than going without; built on the spot (build_s, carpenters hammering) then worked by their crews: wind (the arm drawn back), load, throw (the arm whips over, the stone flies on an arc), settle; every_s between throws; per kind (the one engine is Meshy's catapult, assets/meshy/catapult, whose arm the import split out as a node named arm) the arm's node, its angles (rest, wind, throw), when in the throw the stone lets go (release) and where on the arm it sits (tip, in the model's own units). A stone lands on the wall where it is doomed (walls.gd aim/strike: the wall's wear is the bridge's damage fact; the demo wall wears with each); with nothing doomed it still comes down on the wall's face glance_h (world units) up and glances off in dust (the wall holds: the breach stays the bridge's); with no wall, inside the town in a puff of dust. per_minute: the throws an engine makes a minute at least once built (tools/siege_activity_probe.gd). crew: men per engine; the walls' archers shoot at them, and a fallen man is replaced from the camp after crew_back_s. parked: a ram and a siege tower waiting in the band (no gate to take them yet).

storm_host._: The storm as a mass (army_field.gd storm(); raised with every siege, its waves at the gap once Freeciv assaults): two hosts of the army's regiments (army.gd battle sides, the painted finish and the knight's clips). men: [besiegers, the holder's] (about 100-200 a regiment; frame cost: the army spike drew 6,000 at about 3 fps, so keep the two together near 1,100 for Mac's 10 fps bar [estimate]). from_wall: where the besiegers' host stands, its middle this far (world units) out from the wall's foot: behind the engines' line (engines.from_wall), clear of them, so the men storm past them to the gap (04-siege; group test 1 found a company standing on the engine); holders_back: how far inside the wall the holder's host stands at first; wave_s: a besieger regiment sent to the gap this often once it's open; front, queue: how far before the gap the front regiment's front stands, and the room between one queued block and the next (each block its own depth further back: army_field.gd _waves); holders_at: how far inside the gap the holder's front row's front stands (its rows block by block behind, three abreast, a block's width and army.gap apart: _block_at); walk, run: paces (world units a second); spread: how far inside the gap the besiegers' first row stands once it's taken (four abreast, block by block behind); the holders run to the town's heart, three abreast. breach_fires: how many houses just inside the first breach catch as it opens (fire.gd breach_fires; breach_in: how far inside the gap, world units, they are looked for; g24: fire arrows alone set none alight). arrows: fire arrows loosed over the wall before and during the storm: every_s, most_flying, speed (units a second), spread (how far round the town's heart they land: on one of the houses within it, fire.gd target; g15: 1.4 at random points, few near a house, nothing burned), catch (the chance one sets the house it lands by alight: fire.gd kindle), most_burning (no more catch once this many houses burn).

wall._: While the wall holds (army_field.gd _siege_beats; Mac 2026-11-15, Oldhall and Saltkeep: most troops just standing; Stronghold Crusader, Total War: a siege works on a beat). Every standing regiment keeps its own beat: beats.<unit or role>, each a stance (an army.json track role: ready, rest, idle, block, cheer...) held s seconds (low, high), never the same twice running; a beat with step walks the regiment step (world units) toward the wall with that stance (shields up) where its ground is free, at most forward_most a side out at once, and back after back_s. first_s: each regiment's first beat comes within this, so none starts in step. volley: the units that loose over the wall, each every volley_s (low, high), arrows a volley on arc over flight seconds; their draw holds draw_s; the regiment the arrows come down on raises shields for shields_s (they fell no one: who falls is the bridge's). probe_s, busy: tools/siege_activity_probe.gd watches this long and wants this share of regiments to change clip or place.

garrison._: The holder's men along the wall at a siege (scene_kinds/siege.gd): men, how many; every, radians apart along the wall; bows, the share of them archers (the rest spearmen); reach, how far (world units) from the siege's wall line the town's own wall walk may stand for them to go up on it (walls.gd walk_toward); with none in reach they stand on the ground behind the line.

hungry._: Once hunger reaches a starved town's walls (its siege.hungry): down, the share of the garrison that sinks down and shoots no more; the rest stand hurting.

approach._: How a great house takes the town once its storm has failed (siege_camp.gd approach; bridge siegecraft.js approach, dug). mine: the mouth in (world units in from the camp line toward the walls), width, height; heap, its spoil's radius at the start, heap_per added each season dug, heap_rise its height to its radius, heap_off how far beside the mouth; sappers and their clips. starve: posts round the whole town (skip, radians either side of the camp's middle left to the camp), out (world units past the camp line), sitters at each fire, watch men standing by it, their clips. bribe: reach (world units) to the gate from the camp, meet (the share of the way from the gate the officer waits), the man's clip and pace, talk_s at the officer, again_s before he comes out again.

works._: The besiegers' works growing season by season (siege_camp.gd works; bridge campaigns.js since): first, the share of the palisade standing in the siege's first season (all of it from the second); trench: from, the season the first trench line is dug, one more each season after; at, each line's distance (world units) in from the camp line toward the walls; span (radians either side of the middle), width, segment (world units).

tents._: pennant_every: every so many tents flies the besieger's pennant on its ridge, pennant tall (world units).

parked._: The ram and the siege tower (siege_camp.gd): parked in the band (from_wall: out from the wall's foot, angles, height, crew), then after roll_after_s pushed by their crew (behind it, world units) at pace (world units a second) up to the wall's outer face (ram_out, tower_out: metres off it); gate_reach: the ram goes to the gate instead when one stands within this far (world units) of the wall at the camp's middle, waiting from_wall out in front of it and battering gate_out (world units) off its middle; the ram draws back swing and drives in every blow_s, each blow a strike on the wall and a burst of dust. engines trail, trail_alpha: the flying stone's dust trail; impact: how big the burst of earth where a stone lands.
